72 points, 4 sites. Each site slides in a straight line from its start (solid) to its target (wire).
Every cluster starts at 18 points and must end at its target size (white tick).
Every frame is a balanced least-squares assignment: its cells are a power diagram,
|x - s|^2 - w, so every boundary is a straight line. Reassigned points swell.
A step = one change of assignment. One step per tick in both panels, so the shorter transition finishes first.
COMBINED is a reconstruction of the abstract's idea, not the authors' algorithm: when a shrinking cluster
hands a point to a growing one, that move counts toward the size change instead of being undone by a return move.
40 random cases: fewer steps in 38, never more, median 20% fewer. This is the median case.
